headline: Shift Data Center Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill aims to make large energy users, such as data centers, responsible for their own grid infrastructure costs, potentially reducing the burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocates, environmental groups, Senator Mark Warner.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Virginia Governor Signs Legislation to Shift Data Center Energy Costs
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed legislation directing regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers, preventing these costs from being unfairly allocated to residential customers. This aims to ensure data centers pay their fair share for energy generation and distribution.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Reporting
short_summary: This legislation requires data centers to report their water consumption, providing transparency and data for future water management policies.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, local governments.
news_headline: Virginia Governor Signs Bills Regulating Data Center Water Use
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed bills, including SB 553, aimed at regulating data centers by requiring utilities to report how much water these facilities consume. This provides clearer insight into local resource use, which has often been private.

headline: Regulate Data Center Siting, Noise
short_summary: This bill establishes guidelines and limits for the location and noise levels of data centers, addressing community concerns about their impact.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, community groups, environmental advocates, historic preservation advocates.
opponents: Data center industry, developers (concerned about permitting delays and added costs).
news_headline: Virginia Bill Mandates Data Center Siting and Noise Assessments
news_summary: HB 153 requires local governments to review potential impacts before approving new large data centers, mandating site assessments for noise on nearby homes and schools. Localities can also request reviews on water, farmland, parks, historic sites, and forests.
